rationale: Tests epidemiological fact — India's share of global TB burden — directly from the epidemiology content block.
Tests understanding of latent TB — a core pathogenesis concept covered in the natural history content block.
Tests the BCG vaccine content block — specifically its intradermal route and the age of administration.
Tests understanding of notification obligations under NTEP — a key prevention/programme concept in the final content block.
Tests structured TB history-taking — the student must identify the cardinal symptom duration threshold from the history content block.
Tests the student's ability to analyse the differential diagnosis process — specifically whether lymphoma should be included for a patient with TB-like features and lymphadenopathy.
Tests interpretation of the Mantoux/PPD test — specifically the correct induration threshold for a positive result in an immunocompromised individual.
Tests understanding of CBNAAT as first-line diagnostic test under NTEP — a central concept in the molecular diagnostics content block.
Tests the student's ability to construct a diagnostic workup sequence — integrating multiple tests appropriately for a clinical scenario.
Tests the correct DS-TB regimen under NTEP — specifically the daily FDC intensive and continuation phase format, avoiding the retired intermittent regimen.
Tests understanding of MDR-TB definition — resistance to both isoniazid and rifampicin — from the DR-TB content block.
Tests understanding of the NTEP programme structure and DOTS — specifically the role of the designated microscopy centre and the treatment supporter.
